title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #13 (Term 1)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these plant parts is usually colourful? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Flower
   C. Stem
   D. Soil

2. In a seedling, what is the correct order of growth? (1 mark)
   A. Root, flower, seed
   B. Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   C. Shoot, seed, root
   D. Leaves, seed, root

3. Why do farmers remove weeds from a crop field? (1 mark)
   A. To harm the crops
   B. So crops get enough water, light and space
   C. To stop rain falling
   D. To make weeds grow

4. Which of these shows a plant reproducing? (1 mark)
   A. A leaf turning green
   B. A root drinking water
   C. A stem getting taller
   D. A bean plant making pods with seeds

5. What does removing waste mean for a plant? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting its own leaves
   B. Sending out roots
   C. Getting rid of things its body does not need
   D. Throwing away its seeds

6. Which part of the plant is usually flat, green and spread out to catch light? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Stem
   C. Seed
   D. Leaf

7. Which of these is NOT a job of the roots? (1 mark)
   A. Holding the plant in the soil
   B. Making fruit
   C. Storing food in some plants
   D. Taking in water

8. A caterpillar changes into a butterfly. Which sign of life does this best show? (1 mark)
   A. Feeding only
   B. Dying
   C. Breathing out
   D. Growing

9. What should you do with a small animal after you observe it? (1 mark)
   A. Give it to a friend
   B. Return it to where you found it
   C. Take it home in your pocket
   D. Squash it

10. Why do animals need to feed? (1 mark)
   A. To make their skin colourful
   B. To make noise
   C. To grow feathers only
   D. To get energy and to grow

11. How many legs does a spider have? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Six
   C. Ten
   D. Eight

12. Why is a spider NOT an insect? (1 mark)
   A. It has feathers
   B. It lives in water
   C. It has a backbone
   D. It has eight legs, not six

13. Why is it important to protect wild animals and their homes? (1 mark)
   A. They do not need food
   B. They can be sold cheaply
   C. They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
   D. They are dangerous to all people

14. Which of these is true about the small intestine? (1 mark)
   A. It chews food
   B. Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
   C. It swallows food
   D. It stores faeces

15. Why is diarrhoea dangerous for young children? (1 mark)
   A. They become taller
   B. They lose water quickly
   C. They grow more teeth
   D. They sleep too much

16. Why should you limit sweets and sugary drinks? (1 mark)
   A. They make you taller
   B. They make teeth stronger
   C. They help digestion
   D. They cause tooth decay

17. What is the correct order of parts food passes through? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach, mouth, gullet, small intestine
   B. Mouth, stomach, gullet, anus
   C. Gullet, mouth, small intestine, stomach
   D. Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine

18. What is constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Having worms
   B. Vomiting
   C. Passing watery faeces
   D. Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty

19. What do teeth do in digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Store waste
   B. Digest food into the blood
   C. Cut and grind food into small pieces
   D. Take back water

20. What does deworming do? (1 mark)
   A. Kills worms in the intestines
   B. Cures a cough
   C. Cleans teeth
   D. Makes food taste better

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give two ways in which animals are different from plants. (2 marks)

22. Explain the dangers of diarrhoea and what should be done to help someone who has it. (5 marks)

23. Why is it wrong to say that a tree is not alive because it cannot walk? (3 marks)

24. Explain why we should care for animals and describe how it can be done at home and at school. (5 marks)

25. Explain why we should wash our hands before eating and after using the toilet. (3 marks)

26. Describe how a bean seed grows into a young plant. (3 marks)

27. State two jobs of the mouth in digestion. (2 marks)

28. Describe how you can care for plants at school and at home. Give five ways. (5 marks)

29. State two functions of roots. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Flower
   Flowers are often brightly coloured.

2. B — Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   The seed starts, a root comes out, then a shoot with leaves.

3. B — So crops get enough water, light and space
   Weeds compete with crops for water, light and room.

4. D — A bean plant making pods with seeds
   Making seeds is reproduction. Growing taller is growth.

5. C — Getting rid of things its body does not need
   Living things must remove waste made in their bodies.

6. D — Leaf
   The flat, green shape of a leaf helps it catch light.

7. B — Making fruit
   Fruits are made from flowers, not by roots.

8. D — Growing
   A caterpillar grows and changes form to become a butterfly.

9. B — Return it to where you found it
   Animals should be returned to their home.

10. D — To get energy and to grow
   Food gives animals energy and materials for growth.

11. D — Eight
   Spiders have eight legs.

12. D — It has eight legs, not six
   Insects have six legs and spiders have eight.

13. C — They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
   Wild animals are part of our environment and bring income through tourism.

14. B — Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
   Absorption takes place there.

15. B — They lose water quickly
   The body loses a lot of water and can become weak.

16. D — They cause tooth decay
   Sugar feeds germs that damage teeth.

17. D — Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine
   Food goes from the mouth down the gullet to the stomach and then the small intestine.

18. D — Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
   Constipation means hard faeces that are difficult to pass.

19. C — Cut and grind food into small pieces
   Chewing makes food smaller.

20. A — Kills worms in the intestines
   Deworming tablets kill worms living in the intestines.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Animals can move from place to place. Animals feed on ready-made food while plants make their own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct difference.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: The body loses water quickly and the person becomes weak, especially young children. They should drink clean water and ORS, rest, see a health worker and keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 3 marks for actions.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plants show life in other ways. They grow, reproduce, respond, remove waste and die. Only some animals walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for stating plants show signs of life, 1 mark for naming signs, 1 mark for saying walking is not a sign needed for all living things.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals give us milk, meat, eggs and honey and help us in work. They are part of nature. We give them food, water, shelter and medical care and we do not hurt them. At school we keep the compound safe for birds.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for ways.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hands may carry germs and worm eggs. Washing removes them and stops them entering the mouth and causing disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs on hands, 1 mark for washing removes them, 1 mark for preventing illness.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: The seed takes in water and a root comes out first and goes down. Then a shoot grows up and opens into leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and seed, 1 mark for root first, 1 mark for shoot and leaves.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Teeth cut and grind food. The tongue moves food and saliva wets it and starts digesting starch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct job.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: Water when dry, weed, do not trample, plant trees, do not pick flowers, put waste in bins, protect from animals (any five).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way up to 5.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: They hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts. Some store food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.
